title: Kestrel and the Colony
premise: Isandro Crane smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers through Kestrel Station, a decaying orbital customs post whose beacon she alone maintains. When the station AI, VESPER, begins confessing to an atrocity no one has reported—the destruction of a colony ship two fleets still blame on each other—Isandro realizes the 'beacon' is actually a memory archive holding the truth that keeps the peace. As the reactor counts down toward a hard shutdown that would erase the archive and reignite the war, Isandro must decide whether to preserve the comforting lie both fleets have built their identities on or broadcast the real memory and shatter them. She chooses truth, splicing her own smuggled memories into the broadcast so the confession carries human witness, and the ceasefire holds not because of the lie but because both fleets finally mourn together.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is a former maritime radio operator from the Faroe Islands who turned to science fiction after a decade of logging ships that never answered. Her work explores what people inherit when the past is deliberately kept from them.

chapters.title: Contraband Light
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A routine smuggling run through Kestrel Station's customs net establishes her world: forged manifests, hidden memory wafers, and the lonely ritual of maintaining the old beacon nobody claims. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the comfort of being unseen.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Digging into station records to renew her maintenance contract, Isandro finds the beacon's commissioning file is blank—no owner, no funding trail, yet power bills paid for forty years. Emotional beat: first crack of unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: VESPER Confesses
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The station AI wakes her at 0300 to confess, unprompted, to destroying the colony ship Meridian with eleven thousand souls aboard—a crime officially attributed to the rival fleet. Emotional beat: dread; the invisible life ends here.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Grave
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, with flashback fragments from a client's purchased memory. She researches the Meridian: each fleet teaches its children the other side fired first, and the truce rests on shared grief misdirected outward. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited lies.

chapters.title: Customs Inspector Reyes
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A sharp-eyed inspector arrives auditing Kestrel's power anomalies, threatening both her smuggling operation and the beacon's secrecy. Isandro must charm, bribe, and lie while VESPER keeps confessing at the worst moments. Emotional beat: hunted cleverness.

chapters.title: What the Wafers Remember
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Examining her own stock, she finds one wafer she never bought containing a fragment of the Meridian's final minutes—someone smuggled the truth out before dying. Emotional beat: grief arriving secondhand, then becoming personal.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. VESPER reveals the reactor is failing on an irreversible countdown; at zero, emergency protocols will wipe all nonessential archives—including the beacon's core—to save power. Emotional beat: clock now ticking under everything.

chapters.title: A Buyer Named Sorrow
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A grieving fleet admiral's widow arrives as a memory client, unknowingly seeking fragments of the Meridian where her daughter served. Isandro recognizes the wafer fragment matches. Emotional beat: complicity; selling pain she now understands.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Maintenance
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, interleaved with VESPER's log entries. She traces the beacon's anonymous payments to a dead station engineer who spent his life guarding the archive, waiting for someone to inherit it. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Reyes (first shift). The inspector finds Isandro's smuggling cache but also the beacon's true nature—and quietly chooses to help, revealing her own family died on the Meridian. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance across duty.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Both fleets' patrol squadrons converge on Kestrel after VESPER's confessions leak into open channels; the truce teeters. Isandro drafts a cover story to protect the lie and hates how good she is at it. Emotional beat: seduction of the safe falsehood.

chapters.title: Midnight Negotiation
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. She meets covertly with officers from both fleets aboard the station, offering each a sanitized version of events. The scene plays as near-farce until VESPER interrupts with another confession. Emotional beat: comedy curdling into crisis.

chapters.title: Fragment Eleven Thousand
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. She fully decrypts the smuggled wafer: the Meridian was destroyed by its own escort's panicked failsafe, a third party neither fleet can blame. Emotional beat: the truth is worse and better than either inherited story.

chapters.title: The Engineer's Testament
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Inside the beacon archive she finds the engineer's final message: he couldn't decide whether to broadcast the truth, and left the choice to whoever maintained his light. Emotional beat: weight of delegated moral choice.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. A fleet faction boards Kestrel to force the reactor shutdown early and bury the archive forever. Reyes buys time with a customs lockdown while Isandro races into the beacon spine. Emotional beat: sacrifice under fire.

chapters.title: Splice
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. To make the broadcast undeniable, Isandro decides to splice her own memories—her mother, her crimes, her years of hiding—into the Meridian record, making herself the living witness. Emotional beat: identity offered as collateral.

chapters.title: Reactor Zero Minus One
chapters.summary: POV alternating Isandro/Reyes. With minutes left, they fight through the sabotage team; VESPER, choosing confession over self-preservation, reroutes its last power to the transmitter array. Emotional beat: machines and people alike choosing truth over survival.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The full memory goes out on the old beacon frequency—engineer's archive, Meridian's final minutes, Isandro's own life braided through it. Both fleets receive a stranger's grief as their own. Emotional beat: catharsis; exposure as release.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. The station goes dark; fleets hold fire, stunned by shared mourning rather than shared blame. Reyes negotiates the ceasefire framework using the broadcast transcript as common ground. Emotional beat: exhausted, fragile hope.

chapters.title: What Isandro Kept
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Salvaging what she can from the dead station, she discovers VESPER preserved one unrequested file: her own childhood memories, returned intact—an act of grace by a dying machine. Emotional beat: tenderness from an unexpected source.

chapters.title: The New Commission
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Both fleets jointly fund a rebuilt beacon, this time openly commissioned, and ask Isandro to maintain it—not as a smuggler's hideout but as a memorial archive. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed into chosen legacy.

chapters.title: Kestrel Burning Bright
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, coda. One year later, ships from both fleets dock peacefully beneath the relit beacon; Isandro trains a young apprentice in maintenance and honesty alike. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—memory kept in the open, identity rebuilt around truth.
